This meeting will be held via teleconference only in order to reduce the risk of spreading
COVID-19 and pursuant to AB 361 and the County of Los Angeles Public Health Officer’s
Order (revised September 22, 2022). All votes taken during this teleconference meeting will
be by roll call vote, and the vote will be publicly reported.

HOW TO VIEW THE MEETING: No physical location from which members of the public may
observe the meeting and offer public comment will be provided. Please view the meeting, which
will be live streamed at https://malibucity.org/video and https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting.

HOW TO PARTICIPATE BEFORE THE MEETING: Members of the public are encouraged
to submit email correspondence to mlinden@malibucity.org before the meeting begins.

HOW TO PARTICIPATE DURING THE MEETING: Members of the public may also speak
during the meeting through the Zoom application. You must first sign up to speak before the item
you would like to speak on has been called and then you must be present in the Zoom conference
to be recognized.

Please visit https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting and follow the directions for signing up to
speak and to download the Zoom application.

  B.  Funding for a Consultant to Educate Malibu Residents Regarding the Proposed
  Ballot Question
  Recommended Action: Provide a recommendation to the City Council to consider
  appropriating $25,000 from the General Fund Undesignated Reserve for
  professional services to develop informational materials to educate Malibu
  residents regarding the proposed local general Transaction and Use Tax (TUT) if
  the Council adopts a resolution calling for the placement of the TUT measure on
  the ballot for the November 8, 2022 General Municipal Election.

  Assistant City Manager Toney presented the report. He stated staff reached out to
  three potential consultants and received quotes.

  In response to Councilmember Pierson, Assistant City Manager Toney explained
  that the selected consultant would use the ballot language to develop materials for
  voters and constituents. He stated everything should be completed by the end of
  September to provide separation between the campaign and the election.

  In response to Councilmember Pierson, Assistant City Manager Toney stated the
  information would be put out on the City’s outlets and the voter roll would be
  utilized.

  In response to Councilmember Uhring, Assistant City Manager Toney stated the
  Council’s role was only to take the action on August 8. City Manager McClary
  stated Councilmembers would not be expected to be advocates for the ballot
  measure. In response to Councilmember Uhring, City Manager McClary stated it
  would be welcomed for Councilmembers to provide any questions or comments
  they received from the public.

MOTION  Councilmember Pierson moved, and Councilmember Uhring seconded a motion to
  recommend that the City Council appropriate $25,000 from the General Fund
  Undesignated Reserve for professional services to develop informational materials
  to educate Malibu residents regarding the proposed local general Transaction and
  Use Tax (TUT) if the Council adopts a resolution calling for the placement of the
  proposed TUT measure on the ballot for the November 8, 2022 General Municipal
  Election. The question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.

Subject:  Funding for Malibu Road Drainage Repair Project

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Provide a recommendation to the City Council on the
appropriation of $56,000 from the General Fund Undesignated Reserve for the repair of
damage to Malibu Road that was caused by the Woolsey Fire and severe storm events.

FISCAL IMPACT: Funding for the Malibu Road Drainage Repair Project was included in
the Adopted Budget for Fiscal Year 2022-2023 in the amount of $130,000. Based upon
construction bids received for this project, an additional appropriation of $56,000 from the
General Fund Undesignated Reserve to Account No. 102-9215-5100.00 (Malibu Road
Drainage Repairs) is needed to perform these repairs. The projected General Fund
Undesignated Reserve on October 3, 2022 is $29.45 million. This project was approved
by the California Governor’s Office of Emergency Services (CalOES), which will reimburse
the City for 75% of the project costs, including the additional funding.

WORK PLAN: This item was included as Item 2m in the Adopted Work Plan for Fiscal
Year 2022-2023.

DISCUSSION: Council Policy #44 requires that all proposed appropriations over $10,000
be reviewed and discussed by the Administration and Finance Subcommittee prior to
being presented to the City Council. The proposed appropriation item will be presented to
the Council at its Regular meeting on October 24, 2022.

On November 9, 2018, the Woolsey Fire burned throughout Malibu, causing excessive
damage to homes, businesses, and public infrastructure. The severe storm events that
followed the fire resulted in significant erosion and damage to Malibu Road. The State of

  Page 1 of 2
  Agenda Item # 3.B.
 California declared a State of Emergency for damages sustained by the Woolsey Fire and
the Winter Storms of 2018-2019 allowing the City to apply for funding to assist in the
repairs of Malibu Road. This project consists of the construction of a new retaining wall
and the repair of the eroded shoulder. The project is intended to address the erosion and
damage to Malibu Road that was caused by the Woolsey Fire and severe storm events.
The proposed retaining wall will only be exposed approximately six inches and will act as
a curb preventing stormwater runoff from flowing down the slope and causing more
erosion (Attachment).

On September 1, 2022, nine contractors submitted construction bids for this project. The
lowest bid was $154,291, which is more than the approved budget for this project
($130,000). Additional appropriation is needed to complete this project and repair the
damage to Malibu Road. Staff recommends that an additional $56,000 be allocated from
the General Fund Undesignated Reserve to execute a construction contract with the low
bidder (Hank Co. Inc. dba MD Engineering) and allow for potential change orders up to
20% of the contract.

This project was approved by CalOES as it relates to the damage caused by the Woolsey
Fire and subsequent storm events. CalOES will reimburse the City 75% of the total project
costs. Staff has verified that CalOES will also reimburse the City for the additional funding
needed for this project.

Subject:  Funding for Comprehensive School Safety Assessment Consultant
  Services

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Provide a recommendation to the City Council on the
appropriation of $66,000 from the General Fund Undesignated Reserve to fund a
Professional Services Agreement for a Comprehensive School Safety Assessment.

FISCAL IMPACT: An appropriation of $66,000 from the General Fund Undesignated
Reserve to Account Number 100-7003-5100-00 (City Manager - Professional Services) is
needed to fund a professional services agreement for a Comprehensive School Safety
Assessment. The projected General Fund Undesignated Reserve at June, 30, 2022 is
$29.45 million.

WORK PLAN: This item was not included in the Adopted Work Plan for Fiscal Year 2022-
2023.

DISCUSSION: Council Policy #44 requires that all proposed appropriations over $10,000
be reviewed and discussed by the Administration and Finance Subcommittee prior to
being presented to the City Council. The proposed appropriation item will be presented to
the Council at its Regular meeting on October 24, 2022.

On June 27, 2022, the City Council directed staff to develop and issue a request for
proposal (RFP) for a school safety assessment. The Council also formed the School
Safety Ad Hoc Committee (Committee) of Mayor Pro Tem Silverstein and Mayor Grisanti
to research school safety issues, and review and provide input on the RFP.

  Page 1 of 2
  Agenda Item # 3.C.
 The RFP was issued on July 15, 2022, in partnership with Santa Monica-Malibu Unified
School District (SMMUSD) and the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department (Sheriff).
The RFP sought qualified firms with broad subject matter expertise and experience in K-
12 school safety to conduct a comprehensive and holistic safety assessment. The
assessment will be inclusive of all K-12 schools in the City and will extend beyond physical
security and safety procedures to include a review and analysis of behavioral health
programs, policies and procedures as well. The closing date for response to the RFP was
August 5, 2022, the City received nine proposals. Funding in the amount of $66,000 will
need to be appropriated to ensure enough resources are available to initiate an agreement
with a consultant.

ATTACHMENTS: None.
